question: The first five year plan of India was based on ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harrod-Domar Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First Five Year Plan:**__

 __
 
• The first Indian prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, presented the First Five-Year Plan to the Parliament of India.
 
• The First Five-year Plan was launched in 1951 which mainly focused on the development of the primary sector.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was based on the **Harrod–Domar model with few modifications.**
 
• The target growth rate was 2.1% annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth; the achieved growth rate was 3.6% the net domestic product went up by 15.
 
• Many irrigation projects were initiated during this period, including the Bhakra, Hirakud, Mettur Dam, and Damodar Valley dams.
 
• At the end of the plan period in 1956, five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were started and The University Grants Commission (UGC) was set up.
 
• Contracts were signed to start five steel plants, which existed in the middle of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
• The plan was quasi-successful for the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Basic information about **planning commission and 5-year plans:**

 
 
• Planning commission** founded: 1950.**
 
• Planning Commission** head**:** Prime Minister**
 
• **First five-year plan **launched: in **1951**
 
• A** total** number of **5-year plans**: **12.**
 
• **Last **five-year plan: **2012 to 2017** (Under PM Manmohan Singh).
 
• Planning Commission** dissolved**: **2014** (By** PM Narendra Modi**).
